title: Poland Says Russian Helicopter Flew Into Its Airspace for 42 Seconds
summary:
Forty-two seconds. That's how long Poland says a Russian military helicopter stayed in its airspace on Wednesday morning. That's about as long as it takes to tie your shoes.

The helicopter, a Mi-8, came from Kaliningrad — a small piece of Russia that sits between Poland and Lithuania. It flew about 300 meters (328 yards) into Poland, near a town called Braniewo. That's roughly the length of three football fields.

Poland is a member of NATO, a group of 32 countries that promise to defend each other. When the helicopter crossed in, Poland sent fighter jets into the sky and put ground forces on alert.

Poland's military said the incident shows "Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defence." Russia didn't comment right away.

This isn't the first time. Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine began, several Russian drones and one unarmed missile have landed in Poland. Last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Russia was planning drone and missile strikes against Poland and other NATO countries on the eastern flank.

Russia denies it wants to attack NATO. But European leaders are worried. French President Emmanuel Macron said France had also been targeted by Russian "hybrid attacks" — things like cyberattacks, sabotage, or misinformation — and promised a response.
why_it_matters: Countries agree on rules about whose sky is whose so that small mistakes don't turn into big fights, and when those rules are tested it can affect everything from soldiers' safety to the prices families pay for energy.

background_read: Kaliningrad is a Russian region on the Baltic Sea that is separated from the rest of Russia by other countries, so Russian planes and ships there are close to NATO neighbours like Poland and Lithuania.
NATO (a group of 32 countries, including the United States and Poland, that promise to defend each other) has a rule that an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all.

That rule has been used only once, after the September 11 attacks on the United States in 2001, and since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, European countries have been watching their borders and skies much more closely.
Article_Structure: WHO: Poland's military, Russia (the helicopter came from Russian territory), and NATO leaders including French President Emmanuel Macron.
WHAT: Poland says a Russian Mi-8 military helicopter flew about 300 meters into Polish airspace for 42 seconds, and Poland scrambled fighter jets.
WHERE: Near the town of Braniewo in Poland, close to Kaliningrad, a Russian region between Poland and Lithuania.
WHY: Poland says it shows Russia is testing NATO's air defences, and it fits a pattern of Russian drones and missiles entering Polish airspace.

perspectives.description: They say Russia keeps testing their defences on purpose, and that NATO must answer firmly so the testing stops.
Russia denies it wants to attack NATO and did not comment right away on this flight, suggesting the concern is exaggerated.
They point out that these incidents have happened several times already, and that the real danger is a mistake or misunderstanding that nobody planned.
